```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

data_dir <- "datasets"

read_singstat_wide <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)

  header_index <- which(
    stringr::str_detect(lines, "^Data\\s*Series\\s*,")
  )[1]

  if (is.na(header_index)) {
    stop("No 'Data Series' header found in: ", path)
  }

  raw <- readr::read_csv(
    path,
    skip = header_index - 1,
    na = c("", "na", "NA", "N.A.", "-"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  raw <- dplyr::rename_with(raw, trimws)
  names(raw)[1] <- "data_series"

  raw |>
    mutate(data_series = stringr::str_squish(data_series)) |>
    filter(!is.na(data_series), data_series != "")
}

to_long_years <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(across(matches("^\\d{4}$"), as.character)) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = matches("^\\d{4}$"),
      names_to = "year",
      values_to = "value"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(year),
      value = readr::parse_number(as.character(value))
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(year))
}

standardise_age_group <- function(x) {
  x |>
    stringr::str_squish() |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("\\s*-\\s*", "-")
}

age_groups <- c(
  "15-19 Years",
  "20-24 Years",
  "25-29 Years",
  "30-34 Years",
  "35-39 Years",
  "40-44 Years",
  "45-49 Years"
)

age_group_colours <- c(
  "15-19 Years" = "#D73027",
  "20-24 Years" = "#FC8D59",
  "25-29 Years" = "#FEE08B",
  "30-34 Years" = "#91CF60",
  "35-39 Years" = "#1A9850",
  "40-44 Years" = "#4575B4",
  "45-49 Years" = "#7B3294"
)

fertility_wide <- read_singstat_wide(file.path(data_dir, "BirthsAndFertilityRatesAnnual.csv"))
lfpr_wide <- read_singstat_wide(file.path(data_dir, "M182201.csv"))

asfr_by_age <- fertility_wide |>
  mutate(age_group = standardise_age_group(data_series)) |>
  filter(age_group %in% age_groups) |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(
    year,
    age_group = factor(age_group, levels = age_groups),
    asfr = value
  ) |>
  filter(year >= 1980, !is.na(asfr)) |>
  arrange(age_group, year)

tfr_annual <- fertility_wide |>
  filter(data_series == "Total Fertility Rate (TFR)") |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(year, tfr = value)

lfpr_female <- lfpr_wide |>
  mutate(
    section = case_when(
      data_series == "Female Resident Participation Rate" ~ "Female",
      data_series %in% c(
        "Total Resident Participation Rate",
        "Male Resident Participation Rate"
      ) ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::fill(section, .direction = "down") |>
  filter(section == "Female", data_series != "Female Resident Participation Rate") |>
  mutate(age_group = standardise_age_group(data_series)) |>
  filter(age_group %in% age_groups) |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(
    year,
    age_group = factor(age_group, levels = age_groups),
    female_lfpr_pct = value
  ) |>
  filter(year >= 1990, !is.na(female_lfpr_pct)) |>
  arrange(age_group, year)

recession_events <- tibble(
  recession = c(
    "1985 recession",
    "Asian Financial Crisis",
    "Global Financial Crisis",
    "COVID-19 recession"
  ),
  year = c(1985, 1998, 2009, 2020)
) |>
  mutate(xmin = year - 0.55, xmax = year + 0.55)

birth_policy_events <- tibble(
  year = c(1984, 1987, 2001, 2004, 2008, 2013),
  policy = c(
    "Graduate Mothers Scheme",
    "Have Three or More policy",
    "Baby Bonus",
    "M&P Package",
    "Enhanced M&P Package",
    "Enhanced M&P Package"
  ),
  label_level = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2)
)

asfr_total_by_year <- asfr_by_age |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(total_asfr = sum(asfr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

lfpr_scale <- max(asfr_total_by_year$total_asfr, na.rm = TRUE) / 100

lfpr_line <- lfpr_female |>
  filter(year >= min(asfr_by_age$year), year <= max(asfr_by_age$year))

p_main <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = recession_events,

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    data = recession_events,

  ) +

    data = birth_policy_events,
    aes(xintercept = year),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = birth_policy_events,
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = Inf,
      label = paste0(year, ": ", policy),
      vjust = if_else(label_level == 1, 1.25, 2.65)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_col(
    data = asfr_by_age,
    aes(x = year, y = asfr, fill = age_group),
    width = 0.82,
    alpha = 0.68
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = lfpr_line,
    aes(x = year, y = female_lfpr_pct * lfpr_scale, group = age_group),
    colour = "ghostwhite",
    linewidth = 2.1,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = lfpr_line,
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = female_lfpr_pct * lfpr_scale,
      colour = age_group,
      group = age_group
    ),
    linewidth = 1.15,
    linetype = "dashed",
    alpha = 0.98,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1980, 2025.6),
    breaks = seq(1980, 2025, 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.005, 0.005))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "ASFR (births per 1,000 women)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . / lfpr_scale,
      name = "Female LFPR (%)",
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.40))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = age_group_colours,
    name = "Age group",
    labels = function(x) str_remove(x, " Years")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = age_group_colours,
    name = "Age group",
    labels = function(x) str_remove(x, " Years")
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(title = "Age group", order = 1, nrow = 1),
    colour = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Singapore fertility and female labour-force participation by age group",
    subtitle = "Stacked bars show ASFR by age group. Dashed lines show female LFPR. Shaded bands mark recessions; dotted lines mark major policies.",
    x = "Year",
    caption = "Associations shown, not causation."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    plot.margin = margin(0, 8, 6, 8)

grads <- readr::read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "M850581_female_university_qualified.csv"))

age_band_stops <- tibble(
  midpoint = c(17, 22, 27, 32, 37, 42, 47),
  colour = c("#D73027", "#FC8D59", "#FEE08B", "#A6D96A", "#1A9850", "#4575B4", "#762A83")
)

age_colour_ramp <- colorRamp(age_band_stops$colour, space = "Lab")

birth_age_to_colour <- function(age) {
  t <- approx(
    age_band_stops$midpoint,
    seq(0, 1, length.out = nrow(age_band_stops)),
    xout = age,
    rule = 2
  )$y
  cols <- age_colour_ramp(t)
  rgb(cols[, 1], cols[, 2], cols[, 3], maxColorValue = 255)
}

first_marriage_wide <- read_singstat_wide(file.path(data_dir, "MedianAgeAtFirstMarriageOfResidentCitizenGroomsAndBridesAnnual.csv"))
first_birth_wide <- read_singstat_wide(file.path(data_dir, "MedianAgeOfMothersAtFirstBirthAnnual.csv"))
family_size_wide <- read_singstat_wide(file.path(data_dir, "ResidentEverMarriedFemalesByAgeGroupAndNumberOfChildrenBornAnnual.csv"))

resident_brides_first_marriage <- first_marriage_wide |>
  filter(data_series == "Resident Brides") |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(year, median_age_first_marriage = value)

resident_first_birth_age <- first_birth_wide |>
  filter(data_series == "Median Age Of Mothers At First Birth For Resident Births") |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(year, median_age_first_birth = value)

family_timing <- bind_rows(
  resident_brides_first_marriage |>
    filter(year >= 1990, year <= 2024) |>
    transmute(year, milestone = "First marriage", median_age = median_age_first_marriage),
  resident_first_birth_age |>
    filter(year >= 1990, year <= 2024) |>
    transmute(year, milestone = "First birth", median_age = median_age_first_birth)
) |>
  mutate(milestone = factor(milestone, levels = c("First marriage", "First birth")))

family_timing_labels <- family_timing |>
  group_by(milestone) |>
  filter(year %in% c(min(year), max(year))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(year, ": ", round(median_age, 1)),
    label_x = if_else(year == min(year), year - 0.8, year + 0.45),
    label_y = case_when(
      milestone == "First marriage" & year == min(year) ~ median_age - 0.25,
      milestone == "First birth" & year == min(year) ~ median_age + 0.25,
      milestone == "First marriage" ~ median_age - 0.18,
      TRUE ~ median_age + 0.18
    ),
    hjust_label = if_else(year == min(year), 1, 0)
  )

p_insight3a <- ggplot(family_timing, aes(x = year, y = median_age, colour = milestone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.25) +
  geom_point(data = family_timing_labels, size = 3.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_label(

    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label, hjust = hjust_label),

family_size_tagged <- family_size_wide |>
  mutate(
    age_group = if_else(str_detect(data_series, "^\\d+\\s*-\\s*\\d+\\s+Years$"), data_series, NA_character_),
    children_born = case_when(
      data_series == "None" ~ "None",
      data_series == "1 Child" ~ "1 child",
      data_series == "2 Children" ~ "2 children",
      data_series %in% c("3 Children", "4 Or More Children", "3 Or More Children") ~ "3 or more children",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::fill(age_group, .direction = "down")

family_size_40_49 <- family_size_tagged |>
  filter(str_detect(age_group, "^40\\s*-\\s*49"), !is.na(children_born)) |>
  to_long_years() |>
  transmute(year, children_born, females = value) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    total_females = sum(females, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_pct = females / total_females * 100
  ) |>
  ungroup()

family_size_selected <- family_size_40_49 |>
  filter(year %in% c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, 2025)) |>
  group_by(year, children_born) |>
  summarise(share_pct = sum(share_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    children_born = factor(
      children_born,
      levels = c("3 or more children", "2 children", "1 child", "None")
    ),
    label = if_else(share_pct >= 7, paste0(round(share_pct, 0), "%"), "")
  )

policy_events <- tribble(
  ~event_year, ~event_label, ~policy_stance,
  1972, "Stop at Two", "Anti-natalist",
  1987, "Have Three or More", "Pro-natalist",
  2001, "Baby Bonus", "Pro-natalist",
  2013, "Marriage and Parenthood package", "Pro-natalist"
)

economic_shocks <- tribble(
  ~shock_year, ~shock_label, ~severity, ~quarters_below_peak,
  1985, "1985", "Severe", 6,
  1998, "1998", "Severe", 6,
  2001, "2001", "Moderate", 5,
  2009, "2009", "Most severe", 6,
  2020, "2020", "Most severe", 4
)

policy_window <- policy_events |>
  crossing(relative_year = -5:10) |>
  mutate(year = event_year + relative_year) |>
  left_join(tfr_annual, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    event_label = factor(
      event_label,
      levels = c("Stop at Two", "Have Three or More", "Baby Bonus", "Marriage and Parenthood package")
    )
  )

shock_window <- policy_events |>
  crossing(economic_shocks) |>
  mutate(
    relative_year = shock_year - event_year,
    recovery_years = quarters_below_peak / 4,
    relative_recovery_end = relative_year + recovery_years,
    event_label = factor(
      event_label,
      levels = c("Stop at Two", "Have Three or More", "Baby Bonus", "Marriage and Parenthood package")
    )
  ) |>
  filter(relative_year <= 10, relative_recovery_end >= -5) |>
  mutate(
    xmin = pmax(relative_year, -5),
    xmax = pmin(relative_recovery_end, 10)
  )

p_insight4 <- ggplot(policy_window, aes(x = relative_year, y = tfr, colour = policy_stance)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = shock_window,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = severity),

  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  geom_label(
    data = shock_window,
    aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = Inf, label = shock_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = 1.2,
    size = 2.8,
    label.size = 0.15,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "grey35"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ event_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Anti-natalist" = "#D95F02", "Pro-natalist" = "#1B9E77")) +
  scale_fill_manual(

      "Severe" = "#8073AC",

  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-5, 0, 5, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Did recessions and policies explain fertility changes?",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = policy year. Shaded bands show economic recovery duration and recession severity.",
    x = "Years from policy",
    y = "TFR",
    colour = "Policy stance",
    fill = "Economic shock severity",
    caption = "Policy and recession markers provide context only. Timing is not causal proof."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## The Story {#the-story .section-divider background-image="images/story-bg.jpg" background-size="cover" background-position="center" background-opacity="0.5"}

<div class="section-number">01</div>

<div class="divider-title">The Story</div>

<div class="divider-subtitle">
  Singapore's fertility decline is not only about fewer births. It is also about who is giving birth, when family formation happens and whether policies coincide with recovery.
</div>

---

## What question are we answering? {.story-slide}

<div class="kicker">Research focus</div>

<div class="story-big">
Why has Singapore's fertility rate kept falling despite policy attention?
</div>

<div class="story-sub">
Our answer is descriptive, not causal: the decline appears alongside later family formation, changing education and labour-force patterns, smaller completed families and uneven policy or recession timing.
</div>

<div class="story-question">
<strong>Main question:</strong> What demographic and social changes are associated with Singapore's persistently low fertility from 1980 to 2025?
</div>

---

## Original Visualisation & Critique {#original-visualisation .section-divider background-image="images/critique-bg.jpg" background-size="cover" background-position="center" background-opacity="0.5"}

<div class="section-number">02</div>

<div class="divider-title">Original Visualisation & Critique</div>

<div class="divider-subtitle">
  The original CNA chart is clear for a news story, but it cannot explain long-term fertility behaviour.
</div>

---

## The original CNA visualisation {.clean-slide}

<div class="two-col">

<div class="image-frame">
  <img src="images/cna_birth_chart.png" alt="Original CNA birth-count chart">
  <div class="caption">Source: CNA birth-count visualisation on Singapore citizen births.</div>
</div>

<div class="side-note">
  <div class="kicker">Original story</div>
  <h3>Annual citizen births fell in the recent decade</h3>
  <p>The chart uses annual birth counts to show that Singapore citizen births dropped, with 2022 highlighted as a low point.</p>
  <p>It is effective as a news graphic, but it does not explain whether the decline came from fertility timing, age structure, labour-force change or family-size behaviour.</p>
</div>

</div>

---

## What the original chart does well {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Visual critique</div>
<h2>It communicates the headline quickly</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="card-grid-4">

<div class="info-card good">
  <div class="num">01</div>
  <h3>Clear message</h3>
  <p>The reader immediately sees that citizen births declined.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card good">
  <div class="num">02</div>
  <h3>Simple encoding</h3>
  <p>Bars and direct labels are easy to read.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card good">
  <div class="num">03</div>
  <h3>Useful for news</h3>
  <p>The short comparison period supports a compact article chart.</p>
</div>

</div>

---

## What the original chart cannot explain {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Visual critique</div>
<h2>The chart shows the outcome, not the underlying pattern</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="card-grid-3">

<div class="info-card bad">
  <div class="num">01</div>
  <h3>Birth counts only</h3>
  <p>Counts are affected by population size and age structure, not only fertility behaviour.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card bad">
  <div class="num">02</div>
  <h3>Short time horizon</h3>
  <p>2012-2022 is too short to explain Singapore's longer fertility transition.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card bad">
  <div class="num">03</div>
  <h3>No driver context</h3>
  <p>It does not show maternal age, female LFPR, education, policy timing, recession context or family-size changes.</p>
</div>

</div>

---

## Proposed Improvements {#proposed-improvements .section-divider background-image="images/improvements-bg.jpg" background-size="cover" background-position="center" background-opacity="0.5"}

<div class="section-number">03</div>

<div class="divider-title">Proposed Improvements</div>

<div class="divider-subtitle">
  We keep the original concern about declining births, but redesign the analysis to explain fertility behaviour more directly.
</div>

---

## From birth counts to fertility behaviour {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Redesign logic</div>
<h2>Each improvement addresses a weakness in the original chart</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="card-grid-3">

<div class="info-card blue">
  <div class="num">01</div>
  <h3>Use ASFR and TFR</h3>
  <p>Move beyond raw birth counts so the visual better reflects fertility behaviour rather than only population size.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card blue">
  <div class="num">02</div>
  <h3>Extend the period</h3>
  <p>Use a 1980-2025 window to show longer fertility transition, not just a short news period.</p>
</div>

<div class="info-card blue">
  <div class="num">03</div>
  <h3>Add context</h3>
  <p>Overlay female LFPR, policy milestones and recessions so the audience can compare fertility movement with key contextual shifts.</p>
</div>

</div>

<div class="story-question">
The improvement is not to add more variables for the sake of it. The goal is to make the main fertility story more explainable and self-contained.
</div>

## Data Engineering Workflow {#engineering-workflow .section-divider background-image="images/workflow-bg.jpg" background-size="cover" background-position="center" background-opacity="0.5"}

<div class="section-number">05</div>

<div class="divider-title">Data Engineering Workflow</div>

<div class="divider-subtitle">
  The workflow standardises raw wide tables into consistent plot-ready datasets.
</div>

---

## Raw to plot-ready {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Pipeline overview</div>
<h2>One reproducible workflow across datasets</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="pipeline">

<div class="pipe-step">
  <div class="step-id">STEP 01</div>
  <h3>Import</h3>
  <p>Read CSV files and locate the true data header.</p>
</div>

<div class="pipe-step">
  <div class="step-id">STEP 02</div>
  <h3>Clean</h3>
  <p>Remove metadata, standardise labels and parse values.</p>
</div>

<div class="pipe-step">
  <div class="step-id">STEP 03</div>
  <h3>Reshape</h3>
  <p>Convert year columns into long format.</p>
</div>

<div class="pipe-step">
  <div class="step-id">STEP 04</div>
  <h3>Join</h3>
  <p>Combine datasets by year only where units are comparable.</p>
</div>

<div class="pipe-step">
  <div class="step-id">STEP 05</div>
  <h3>Validate</h3>
  <p>Check expected year ranges, age groups and missing values.</p>
</div>

</div>

---

## Raw layouts and cleaning needs {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Data engineering detail</div>
<h2>The raw files did not all arrive in analysis-ready form</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="engineering-card-grid">

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">01</div>
  <h3>Metadata rows</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> detect the true <code>Data Series</code> header before reading.</p>
  <span>Prevents metadata from becoming fake observations.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">02</div>
  <h3>Wide year columns</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> pivot years into long format.</p>
  <span>Allows filtering, joining and plotting by year.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">03</div>
  <h3>Inconsistent labels</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> standardise age groups such as <code>20-24 Years</code>.</p>
  <span>Ensures ASFR and LFPR age bands match.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">04</div>
  <h3>Mixed value types</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> parse numeric values after reshaping.</p>
  <span>Prevents text values from breaking calculations.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">05</div>
  <h3>Different ranges</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> keep available years and show honest gaps.</p>
  <span>Avoids inventing observations for missing periods.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">06</div>
  <h3>Event context</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> create manual policy and recession event tables.</p>
  <span>Keeps annotations reproducible and separate from measured data.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">07</div>
  <h3>Different units</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> keep ASFR, TFR, LFPR, ages and percentages clearly separated.</p>
  <span>Avoids misleading comparisons across incompatible measures.</span>
</div>

<div class="engineering-card">
  <div class="eng-num">08</div>
  <h3>Derived measures</h3>
  <p><strong>Fix:</strong> compute shares, policy-relative years and visual encodings.</p>
  <span>Turns raw data into story-ready variables.</span>
</div>

</div>

---

## Engineering transformations and checks {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Reproducibility and validation</div>
<h2>Key transformations used before plotting</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="schema-grid">

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Year alignment</h3>
  <p>All tables were joined by <code>year</code>. No row was joined by position.</p>
</div>

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Age-group matching</h3>
  <p>ASFR and LFPR age bands were standardised before plotting together.</p>
</div>

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Policy windows</h3>
  <p>TFR was converted to years before and after policy years for fair comparison.</p>
</div>

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Family-size shares</h3>
  <p>Counts of children born were converted into percentages within each year.</p>
</div>

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Visual encodings</h3>
  <p>Size, colour and shaded bands were derived from clean numeric variables.</p>
</div>

<div class="schema-card">
  <h3>Validation checks</h3>
  <p>Checked expected year ranges, missing values, age groups and percentage totals.</p>
</div>

</div>

## Insights & Analysis {#insights-analysis .section-divider background-image="images/insightsanalysis-bg.jpg" background-size="cover" background-position="center" background-opacity="0.5"}

<div class="section-number">07</div>

<div class="divider-title">Insights & Analysis</div>

<div class="divider-subtitle">
  Four supporting insights answer what changed underneath the fertility decline.
</div>

---

## Insight 1: Education, LFPR and birth timing {.clean-slide}

::: {.two-col}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_insight1
```

::: {.side-note}
<div class="kicker">Insight 1</div>
<h3>Education, work participation and later birth timing moved together</h3>
<p>Female university attainment rose strongly from 1990 to 2025.</p>
<p>The same period also shows higher female LFPR and later median age at first birth.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> this supports the idea that women's pathway into adulthood increasingly involved higher education and work before motherhood.</p>
:::

:::

---

## Insight 2: Longer schooling and younger-age fertility {.clean-slide}

::: {.two-col}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_insight2
```

::: {.side-note}
<div class="kicker">Insight 2</div>
<h3>Younger adulthood shifted toward schooling</h3>
<p>Female literacy and schooling increased, while LFPR for ages 15 to 24 weakened.</p>
<p>This is especially clear for ages 15 to 19, where participation became much lower.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> this helps explain why births among women aged 15 to 19 and 20 to 24 became much less important in the main visualisation.</p>
:::

:::

---

## Insight 3A: Family formation moved later {.clean-slide}

::: {.two-col}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_insight3a
```

::: {.side-note}
<div class="kicker">Insight 3A</div>
<h3>Family formation shifted later</h3>
<p>Median age at first marriage increased from the mid-20s toward the late-20s.</p>
<p>Median age at first birth also moved upward, reaching the early-30s by the latest years.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Singapore's low fertility is partly about delayed entry into marriage and parenthood, not only fewer births in one year.</p>
:::

:::

---

## Insight 3B: Completed family size became smaller {.clean-slide}

::: {.two-col}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_insight3b
```

::: {.side-note}
<div class="kicker">Insight 3B</div>
<h3>Later family formation connects to smaller completed families</h3>
<p>Among ever-married women aged 40 to 49, larger families became less common.</p>
<p>Smaller family-size categories became more prominent over time.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> this connects delayed family formation to the longer-term TFR decline because fewer families end up having three or more children.</p>
:::

:::

## Insight 4: Policy and recession timing {.clean-slide}

::: {.two-col}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 5.2
p_insight4
```

::: {.side-note}
<div class="kicker">Insight 4</div>
<h3>Policy and recession timing give context, not causal proof</h3>
<p>Some policy periods coincide with short-term changes, but no sustained recovery appears.</p>
<p>Recession bands help show economic timing around policy windows.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> policy matters, but fertility decline remains a broader structural pattern.</p>
:::

## Limitations {.clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Interpretation boundaries</div>
<h2>What we can and cannot claim</h2>
<div class="hr-accent"></div>

<div class="limit-grid">

<div class="limit-card">
  <h3>Association, not causation</h3>
  <p>Policies, recessions and social indicators are used as timing context. They do not prove a direct cause.</p>
</div>

<div class="limit-card">
  <h3>Different measures</h3>
  <p>ASFR, TFR, LFPR, education and age measures use different units, so we avoid forcing them onto one scale unless clearly labelled.</p>
</div>

<div class="limit-card">
  <h3>Period versus cohort</h3>
  <p>TFR describes fertility in a year, while completed family size describes older cohorts. Both are useful, but they answer different questions.</p>
</div>

</div>

---

## Conclusion {#conclusion .clean-slide}

<div class="kicker">Final takeaway</div>

<div class="conclusion-big">
Singapore's fertility decline appears to be a <span>long-term structural pattern</span>, not a drop caused by one isolated policy, recession or demographic change.
</div>

<div class="story-question">
The clearest story is cumulative: younger-age fertility weakened, female education and LFPR rose, family formation shifted later and completed families became smaller. Policy matters, but it operates within these broader social and demographic shifts.
</div>
